title: Heat Pump Rebates in Thunder Bay 2026: A -14C January and Cold-Climate Rules
desc: Thunder Bay heat pump rebates for 2026 under Home Renovation Savings: 73% of homes predate 1981, January lows average -14.2C and cold-climate performance is required.
h1: Heat Pump Rebates in Thunder Bay
badge: Up to $7,500 for an air-source heat pump
lead: Thunder Bay averages -14.2°C in January and has reached -31.9°C. The program only pays for cold-climate models, and the rate depends on your current fuel.
cards_heading: What Home Renovation Savings pays for a heat pump in Thunder Bay
cards_intro: We re-read the program's heat pump page and its requirements document on October 3, 2026. No home energy assessment is needed for this stream, but a participating HVAC contractor and written pre-approval are.

cards.title: Air-source, electric, oil, propane or wood heat
cards.note: For a cold-climate air-source heat pump replacing electric resistance, oil, propane or wood as the main heat. A 3-ton system pays $3,750 and 6 tons or more reaches the cap.

cards.title: Air-source, Enbridge gas heat
cards.note: For homes primarily heated by an Enbridge gas furnace or boiler. The cap is reached at 4 tons.

cards.title: Ground-source
cards.note: For electric, oil, propane or wood homes. Gas homes get a flat $3,000. The system must be a full installation sized to the home's load.

cards.title: Rented heat pump
cards.note: Rentals are eligible for any primary heating fuel: $500 per ton for air-source, up to $2,000, or a flat $3,000 for ground-source.

cards.title: More than one outdoor unit
cards.amount: Up to three units, one rebate
cards.note: If several outdoor units are needed to heat the whole home, their tons add up and one rebate is paid on the total, for example 3 + 3 tons for $7,500.

cards.title: One rebate, pre-approved
cards.note: One rebate per home. The contractor needs written pre-approval before installing, files the post-installation application within 30 days, and the cheque arrives within 60 days of approval.

after_cards: The requirements document lists no end date, but the program's other streams close in late 2026, so check the program page before you sign a contract. Pre-approval is mandatory: an installation done first earns nothing.
sections: The 2021 Census counts 21,420 owner-occupied detached houses built before 1981, 73% of households in homes of that age, 73% in an eligible house type and 68% owning. 7.6% report needing major repairs. 16% live in low-rise apartments and 2,390 in duplexes.

Electric, oil and wood homes must choose NRCan sizing option C or D. In Thunder Bay's climate that is the sensible choice anyway, because a system sized mainly for cooling would leave the backup working hard. Ask the contractor to share the NRCan sizing form so you can see the design load and the capacity at design temperature.

Ground-source pays $2,000 per ton up to $12,000 for electric, oil, propane and wood homes. It must be sized to the full heating load and installed as a complete system, with direct-expansion not allowed. With a January low of -14.2°C, stable ground temperatures help, but lot and soil conditions decide feasibility.

The Energy Affordability Program from Save on Energy offers free upgrades to income-qualified households. Its comprehensive support can include cold-climate heat pumps for oil-heated homes, so an eligible household should check it before paying for a heat pump or applying for a rebate.
The approval comes before the crew

The participant agreement is accepted only if the pre-installation application is approved in writing. An installation done before approval earns nothing. A Thunder Bay owner with a short building season should schedule the approval first, because a delay in paperwork can push the install into winter.

The contractor files within 30 days with the final itemized invoice, photos of the installed equipment and thermostat, and measure details. The cheque arrives within 60 days of approval. Keep copies of the invoice and approval.
claim_heading: How to claim in Thunder Bay
claim_steps: Ask for the NRCan sizing form before you choose a contractor.
Confirm eligibility on the program's short form and get the list of participating HVAC contractors.
Choose a contractor from that list. Ask for a load calculation and the NRCan sizing tool form for each outdoor unit.
Wait for written pre-approval before any installation starts.
After the install, check that the contractor files the post-installation application within 30 days, with the final itemized invoice and photos.
